review_items.title: Work Order → incurs → Cost Line
review_items.detail: L/S/T match — lexical 0.88 · structural 0.79 · type 0.76 · evidence: AUFK.AUFNR joins WORKORDER_COSTS on 96.2% of sampled rows. Prior: you approved the same pattern in Service Interruptions (decision memory).

review_items.title: Interruption → caused-by → Pump cavitation
review_items.detail: Causal claims always see a human. Evidence: incident narrative #88 names cavitation; work orders WO-2201/2214 follow within 72h. Correlational alternative available.

review_items.title: Contractor
review_items.detail: Proposed from new Hexagon EAM column contractor_id plus contract signatories. Adding an entity type changes the schema → floor review.

review_items.title: Change Order → revises → Authorization
review_items.detail: Extraction-derived. Links a contract clause to a financial authorization — crossing from unstructured to ledger always sees a human.

pivot.title: Entity resolution: Contractor vs Vendor
pivot.detail: Hexagon EAM contractor_id and the ledger's vendor_no overlap on 71% of rows. Resolving them as one entity changes what every other decision in this queue means, so the queue cannot be read until it is settled.

options.label: One entity — Contractor absorbs Vendor
options.consequence: Cost lines and work orders share one counterparty; 3 approved relationships are re-scoped.

options.label: Two entities — keep Vendor separate
options.consequence: Ledger stays independent of EAM; the Contractor → performs → Work Order edge is dropped.
